newsitem.title: USA: Great Western insiders disclose stock sale plans.
newsitem.headline: Great Western insiders disclose stock sale plans.

text.p: Great Western Financial Corp chairman James Montgomery filed a notice with the Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) that he intends to sell shares on the same day H.F. Ahmanson and Co announced an unsolicited bid for the company.

According to a Form 144 filing, Montgomery exercised options to acquire 114,000 shares and said he was giving notice of his intention to sell the shares. His filing was made on February 18, which was the day Ahmanson announced its bid for Great Western.
The form also disclosed that Montgomery sold 50,000 shares on January 24, 1997, collecting gross proceeds of $1,597,941.
Great Western Chief executive John Maher made a Form 144 filing on February 24 in which he said he intended to sell 6,155 shares acquired through the exercise of an option.
A spokesman for Great Western was not immediately available for comment.

A Wall Street arbitrager said that, while the filings could have been a coincidence, it was more likely the two men wanted to be in a position to sell their stock. Corporate insiders must comply with various technical requirements when they sell stock.
A source close to Ahmanson, however, argued that the two were looking out for their own interests, while Great Western has not yet adopted an official stance on the Ahmanson bid.
Great Western has been rumoured to be trying to line up a "white knight" suitor to rival the Ahmanson bid, which Wall Steet views as a hostile takeover attempt.
Ahmanson has proposed acquiring Great Western in a stock deal worth about $6 billion. Holders of Great Western would get 1.05 shares of Ahmanson for each Great Western share.
